authors: Zihao Yang; Tianyi Qu; Xinran Li
title: Rejective Sampling, Rerandomization and Regression Adjustment in Survey Experiments
venue_or_arxiv: arXiv:2109.09930; J. Amer. Statist. Assoc. 118(542), 1207-1221 (2023) per IDEAS listing
what_it_holds: Two-stage design for survey experiments. Sampling stage draws a simple random sample of units and accepts it only if the Mahalanobis distance between sample and population covariate means is below a threshold a_S (Morgan-Rubin style applied to sampling); treatment stage rerandomises similarly. Gives asymptotic theory, regression-adjusted estimators and regression-based variance estimators (Sec. 5.2), conservative when design information is not used. Sampling units are individuals, not clusters; covariates are generic, not predictions; no t reference or v_a shrinkage was confirmed from what I read (abstract and summary page).

title: Some design properties of a rejective sampling procedure
what_it_holds: Rejective procedure that keeps a sample only if the sample mean of an auxiliary vector is within a set distance of the population mean. Shows that in large samples the regression estimator and its usual variance estimator keep their original-design properties under rejection; Monte Carlo at small sizes. Units are generic sampling units, not clusters, and the auxiliary variable is not a prediction.  [from abstract only]

authors: Jason C. Legg; Cindy L. Yu
title: A comparison of sample set restriction procedures
full_text_open: yes (journal open access; abstract read only)
what_it_holds: Stratified random sampling with rejection of samples whose estimates of known quantities fall outside a tolerance; modifies Fuller's 2009 rejection rule to be more flexible. Simulations compare rejective sampling with cube sampling, which is the only place the two designs of C5 and C6 meet in what I found.  [from abstract only]

title: Two-phase rejective sampling and its asymptotic properties
venue_or_arxiv: J. R. Stat. Soc. Series B 2025, 957-977 (DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkaf002)
what_it_holds: Rejective sampling with auxiliary information measured in a first phase and rejection applied to the second phase; asymptotics for double-expansion and regression estimators, extension to multi-phase and estimating equations. States that asymptotic theory for single-phase rejective sampling had not been fully established. Units are individuals; no clusters and no predictions as balance variables.  [from abstract only]

authors: Xin Lu; Tianle Liu; Hanzhong Liu; Peng Ding
title: Design-based theory for cluster rerandomization
what_it_holds: Cluster-randomised experiments with rerandomisation: acceptance by Mahalanobis distance of cluster-level or individual-level covariate means below threshold a, with chi-square guidance for a. Treatment assignment of clusters, not sampling of clusters. Regression-adjusted estimators with cluster-robust (Liang-Zeger) or Huber-White standard errors, conservative under rerandomisation. Closest analogue to the cluster structure but for assignment, not selection for labelling.

title: Non-asymptotic bounds for inclusion probabilities in rejective sampling
what_it_holds: Here rejective sampling means conditional Poisson sampling (fixed size). Gives non-asymptotic bounds on first-order and higher-order inclusion probabilities and on the matrix of first and second-order probabilities. Bears on C7 only indirectly, since it concerns conditional Poisson, not Mahalanobis-acceptance rejection.

title: Conservative variance estimation for sampling designs with zero pairwise inclusion probabilities
what_it_holds: Horvitz-Thompson variance estimation when some pairwise inclusion probabilities are zero ('non-measurable' designs). Breaks down the standard estimator's bias and proposes an always weakly conservative correction. Directly relevant to the failure mode in C7 and to a possible fix.  [from abstract only]

title: Doubly balanced spatial sampling with spreading and restitution of auxiliary totals
what_it_holds: Spreads units in space and balances auxiliary totals so the HT estimates match known values; any distance, unequal probabilities; compared with local pivotal, cube and GRTS and gives a variance estimator. Units are individual locations, sample sizes not stated in what I read.  [from abstract only]

authors: Raphael Jauslin; Bardia Panahbehagh; Yves Tille
title: Sequential Spatially Balanced Sampling
what_it_holds: Selects a balanced, well-spread sample one unit at a time. Section 6 uses the Deville-Tille (2005) residual-based approximation for balanced designs and nearest-neighbour or combined spatial variance estimators; notes these estimators do poorly for unequal-probability balanced designs because of the rounding problem and that second-order inclusion probabilities are generally unknown. Read via text extract of the PDF.

title: Ten years of balanced sampling with the cube method: An appraisal
what_it_holds: Review of balanced sampling and the cube method: history, theory, comparison with other designs and calibration, accuracy of balancing, choice of auxiliary variables, implementation.  [from abstract only]

title: Probability Sampling Designs: Principles for Choice of Design and Balancing
what_it_holds: Formalises randomisation, overrepresentation and restriction as design principles within a model-assisted framework, and reviews balanced sampling and spatial methods with an example. Variance estimation and rejective sampling not mentioned in the abstract.  [from abstract only]

authors: Caren Hasler; Esther Eustache; Yves Tille
title: In Search of the Most Balanced Sampling Design
what_it_holds: Genetic-algorithm heuristic for the most balanced design at fixed inclusion probabilities, can improve on the cube method; for very small populations exact linear programming is possible. Variance estimation and joint inclusion probabilities not mentioned in the abstract.  [from abstract only]

title: With-Replacement Balanced Sampling
venue_or_arxiv: Scandinavian Journal of Statistics (DOI 10.1111/sjos.70091; journal inferred from ISSN 0303-6898)
what_it_holds: Three generalised-cube algorithms for with-replacement balanced designs and a variance approximation tested by simulation. Not about without-replacement cluster selection.  [from abstract only] Check the publication month against the 1 September 2026 flag.

title: PPI is the Difference Estimator: Recognizing the Survey Sampling Roots of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Argues the PPI mean estimator is algebraically the difference estimator of Cassel et al. (1976) and PPI+ is the GREG estimator. Suggests survey tools (calibration, optimal allocation, design-based diagnostics) for PPI. No cluster selection design proposed in the abstract.  [from abstract only]

title: Design-Based Prediction-Powered Inference for Spatial Data
what_it_holds: Census parameter of a fixed spatial population of pixels, randomness from labelling. Phase-two probability sample of n units under simple, stratified, one-per-block and spatially balanced designs (GRTS, local pivotal). Two-phase difference estimator with HT and Hajek forms, power tuning, sandwich variance for estimated propensities. Selection may depend on map-derived quantities (map value, uncertainty score), treated as ignorable, so predictions guide selection, but units are pixels, not clusters, and I did not see rejective or cube designs. Read from the arXiv HTML summary, formulas not seen.

title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Cluster-Robust PPI++ with closed-form standard errors under arbitrary within-cluster dependence, including partially labelled clusters. Analyses how the labelling design affects precision and gives a cluster-aware power tuning rule. Model-based asymptotics with many independent clusters, not finite-population design-based inference with a few selected clusters. After 1 September 2026.  [from abstract only]

title: M-estimation under Two-Phase Multiwave Sampling with Applications to Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Already recorded. Two-phase multiwave design with adaptive labelling of subsets, Multiwave Predict-Then-Debias estimator, approximately greedy sampling, asymptotic linearity. Units are individuals.  [from abstract only]

authors: Boyu Chen; Zhixiang Zhou; Liuhua Peng; Zhonglei Wang
title: Balanced Active Inference
what_it_holds: Already recorded. Adds balance constraints based on model uncertainty and selects labels by the cube method, with asymptotics and nominal coverage in experiments. Units are individual instances, asymptotic framework. No forward citation found that adds cluster-level use.  [from abstract only]

authors: Virginia L. Ma; Emmanuel J. Candes
title: Optimized Labeling Resource Allocation for Prediction-Assisted Inference via OPAL
what_it_holds: Learns a soft labelling policy pi(X) from model uncertainty to minimise variance; Bernoulli labelling per unit with an expected budget, AIPW estimator, group-specific policies for two groups. Units are individuals; clusters are not treated. Read from the HTML text.

authors: Authors not confirmed from the page read (NeurIPS 2025; ML Anthology key suggests first author Li)
title: Robust Sampling for Active Statistical Inference
what_it_holds: Moves the active sampling rule along a budget-preserving path toward uniform sampling with the mixing weight chosen by estimated variance; the minimax version guards against unreliable uncertainty. Independent Bernoulli sampling of individual instances, inverse-probability-weighted residual correction. Read only through a third-party summary (the arXiv page was blocked by permissions). This is the closest relative of mixing a label-free score with uniform probabilities (C6).

authors: Henrik Imberg and co-authors (author list not confirmed)
title: Active sampling: A machine-learning-assisted framework for finite population inference with optimal subsamples
what_it_holds: Finite-population inference with batches drawn with replacement under a multinomial design, probabilities set by a model (proportional to p_i times sqrt of a model-based variance term, density fallback). Hansen-Hurwitz estimator and three variance estimators including pooled Sen-Yates-Grundy. Units are instances, not clusters. Read from a text extract of the PDF.

authors: Yilin Song; Dan M. Kluger; Harsh Parikh; Tian Gu
title: Demystifying Prediction Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Review of PPI with a workflow and diagnostics. IID framing, labelling missing at random; Sec. 3.2 on survey sampling approaches exists but was not visible to me. Not a clustered or design-based treatment.  [from abstract only]
